To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a time dependent toxicodynamic model for mixture toxicity was developed to predict mixture toxicity with toxicodynamic interactions.
the DAM can be extended to a multiconponent model for mixture toxicology and can be used to describe and predict the time dependent toxic effects of a mixture with biotransformation interactions.
the time dependent toxicity and biotransformation of organic compounds can be described and predicted with the DAM and its multicomponent extensions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model to predict the time-dependent toxicity of a mixture of chemicals.
developing a new toxicokinetic model for predicting the time dependent mixture toxicity of organic compounds with toxicokinetic and toxicodynamic interactions.
understanding the toxicokinetic toxicodynamics of a chemical mixture and the role of metabolism in the toxicity of a mixture.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this model can be used to predict mixture toxicity of compounds with biotransformation and/or biotransformation inhibition.
the DAM was extended to the MDAM and the MDAM was used to predict the time-dependent toxicity of a mixture of two chemicals, each with a toxicologically active metabolite.

the MDAM provides a framework to assess the role that biotransformation plays in the toxicity of organic compounds and provides a basis for the development of a more general model for mixture toxicity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed and validated the first time dependent toxicokinetic model for the assessment of the toxicity of mixtures with toxicokinetic and toxicodynamic interactions.

the DAM and its extensions can describe the time dependent toxic effects of a single compound or a mixture of compounds, and that it is a useful model for predicting and interpreting the toxic effects of organic mixtures with biotransformation and toxicokinetic interactions.
the DAM can be extended to a multiconponent DAM to predict mixture toxicity and that the multicomponent model is applicable to compounds with potentially dissimilar mode of actions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the toxicokinetic and toxicodynamic parameters of the DAM can be used to describe and predict the time dependent mixture toxicity of a chemical mixture with toxicokinetics interactions, and that a toxic unit model can be derived from the multicomponent version of DAM to assess the relative contribution of each mixture component to the mixture toxicity.
the multicomponent model can be applied to assess the role that biotransformation plays in the toxicity of a mixture.
the DAM can be used as a tool to assess the role that toxicokinetic interactions have on the toxicity of a chemical.
